title: Initialize Fedo at app startup
description: Add an Application class (registered in the manifest) that calls Fedo.initialize(applicationContext, apiKey) once in onCreate when the BuildConfig key is non-blank, with debug logging enabled only in debug builds. When the key is blank, skip initialization and log one clear hint naming local.properties. Keep a single accessor for "is Fedo configured" that the UI can reuse.
acceptance_criteria: With a key the SDK initializes; without one the app runs, logs the hint and never crashes.
close_reason: ModelPulseApplication registered in the manifest; both paths verified on a Pixel 10 emulator - no key logs the hint and stays up, with a key initialization runs and the hint is absent. Neither crashes. Unit tests cover the blank-key logic.

title: Load the Fedo API key from gitignored local.properties
description: The key must never be committed. Read FEDO_API_KEY from local.properties (gitignored) in the app build script and expose it as a BuildConfig field, defaulting to an empty string so a clean clone and CI still build. Document the setup in a tracked example file or comment (e.g. local.properties.example) pointing at the Fedo dashboard at https://app.getfedo.com.
acceptance_criteria: Clean clone builds with no key (BuildConfig field empty); with a key in local.properties the field carries it; no key in git.
close_reason: BuildConfig.FEDO_API_KEY empty on a clean clone, carries the key when local.properties sets it; both paths verified against the generated BuildConfig.java. local.properties stays gitignored; local.properties.example documents it.

title: Configure the app module and add the Fedo SDK
description: Add the Fedo dependency (com.getfedo:sdk-android:0.4.0 - confirm the repository it resolves from: mavenCentral or a Fedo maven URL) via the version catalog. Set the app name to ModelPulse, confirm minSdk/targetSdk/compileSdk and Java/Kotlin toolchain build, enable BuildConfig generation (needed for the API key), and keep Material 3 + Compose BOM from the template. Do not add third-party libraries beyond the SDK, a JSON library and an HTTP client if needed.
acceptance_criteria: ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug succeeds with the SDK on the classpath; app label shows ModelPulse.
close_reason: SDK on debugRuntimeClasspath, assembleDebug/testDebugUnitTest/lintDebug all pass, app label is ModelPulse, BuildConfig generation on.

title: Commit the generated project skeleton with clean ignores
description: The repo currently has only the bd init commit; the whole generated Compose project (app/, gradle/, build.gradle.kts, settings.gradle.kts, gradlew) is untracked. Commit it, and make sure .gitignore covers the things that must never be tracked: build/, .gradle/, .idea/ (except shared parts if wanted), .kotlin/, local.properties, *.apk, captures/. Keep the beads entries already in .gitignore.
acceptance_criteria: git status is clean after a build; git ls-files shows no build output, no local.properties, no IDE state.
close_reason: Skeleton committed in a718c07 with a rewritten .gitignore: .idea/ ignored wholesale, .kotlin/ added, duplicate local.properties entry removed. git ls-files shows no build output, no local.properties, no IDE state.

title: Project setup
description:
Get the fresh Compose project into a correct, reproducible, committed state and wire up the Fedo SDK.

Fedo Android SDK 0.4.0 API (docs: https://docs.getfedo.com/next/guide/getting-started/):
  implementation("com.getfedo:sdk-android:0.4.0")
  Fedo.initialize(applicationContext, apiKey = "...") { timeoutInMillis = 10_000; debug = true }  // once, before any other call
  Fedo.setUserID / setUserDisplayName / setUserEmail / setUserProperty(key, value) / logout()
  FedoFeedbackScreen(onDismiss = { }, slots = FedoFeedbackScreenDefaults.slots())  // full board, hosted in your Compose hierarchy
  FedoCreateFeedbackSheet(onDismiss = { })                                          // submission-only bottom sheet
Uninitialized SDK: Android throws IllegalStateException from the sheet and the screen shows a not-initialized state, so the app must guard its own UI when no key is configured.

title: Fedo SDK 0.4.0 ships its test dependencies to consumers
description:
com.getfedo:sdk-android:0.4.0 declares kotlin-test, kotlin-test-junit and ktor-client-mock at runtime scope in its published POM. They resolve onto debugRuntimeClasspath and are dexed into the APK, which comes to about 46 MB. The cause is in the SDK's publication (kusa-software/fedo-sdk) - those should be testImplementation, not implementation or api. Proper fix is an SDK release; this repo can only exclude them. See specs/decisions/0001-library-versions.md for the exclude block.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Add implementation("com.getfedo:sdk-android:0.4.0") to app/build.gradle.kts.
2. Run ./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration debugRuntimeClasspath - kotlin-test, kotlin-test-junit and ktor-client-mock appear.
3. Run ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug, unzip the APK, grep the dex files for Lorg/junit/Assert; and engine/mock/MockEngine; - both are present (classes8.dex and classes7.dex respectively).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: no org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-test, kotlin-test-junit or io.ktor:ktor-client-mock appears in ':app:dependencies --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath'. AC-2: no Lorg/junit/ or MockEngine class is present in the release APK's dex. AC-3: either the SDK is bumped to a release that fixes the publication, or the exclusions are in app/build.gradle.kts with a comment linking this bead.
notes:
Verified 2026-09-21 by adding the SDK to this project and scanning the assembled debug APK. Upstream repo: https://github.com/kusa-software/fedo-sdk
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Add `implementation("com.getfedo:sdk-android:0.4.0")` to app/build.gradle.kts.
2. Run `./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration debugRuntimeClasspath` — kotlin-test, kotlin-test-junit and ktor-client-mock appear.
3. Run `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`, unzip the APK and grep the dex files for `Lorg/junit/Assert;` and `engine/mock/MockEngine;` — both are present.

title: Add the OpenRouter response test fixture
description: specs/testing.md requires a trimmed real OpenRouter response at app/src/test/resources/models.json for decoding tests. It does not exist yet. Capture a real GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models response and trim it to a handful of entries that cover the awkward cases the decoder has to survive.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: app/src/test/resources/models.json exists and decodes with the production Json config. AC-2: the fixture includes a '~'-prefixed id, a null context_length, a '0' price, a '-1' price, and an entry with no architecture object.

title: Spec the Fedo SDK showcase surface
description: The Fedo showcase epic describes three surfaces (roadmap board, contextual feedback sheet, settings with demo sign-in) but nothing states how they fit together or how they behave when the SDK is not usable. Decide and write down: where the roadmap destination sits in the Navigation 3 back stack; what 'demo sign-in' does and which user fields it sets; what the app shows when local.properties has no Fedo API key (the repo must stay clonable and runnable without one); whether SDK failures surface to the user or are swallowed. Put it in specs/ alongside the other project rules.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: a spec states the placement of each Fedo surface and its entry point. AC-2: the missing-API-key behaviour is specified and does not crash or block the rest of the app. AC-3: demo sign-in names the exact Fedo user fields it sets.

title: Manual QA against a real Fedo board
description: With a real API key in local.properties, verify end to end: the board loads, creating feedback works, voting and commenting work, the submission sheet posts, signing in migrates guest activity to the account, signing out starts a new guest, and the favorite_provider property appears in the dashboard. File anything broken as new beads.
acceptance_criteria: All Fedo flows verified with a real key; findings filed.

title: Add the license
description: MIT, matching the iOS example (Copyright 2026 Fedo). Note in the README that the Fedo SDK itself is distributed under its own license.
acceptance_criteria: LICENSE committed and linked from the README.

title: Settings screen with demo sign-in and SDK status
description:
Settings shows whether Fedo is configured (and how to configure it), plus a demo account section with a name/email form. Signing in calls setUserID, setUserDisplayName and setUserEmail; signing out calls logout. Persist the demo user locally so the state survives restarts. Explain in the UI that feedback, votes and comments made as a guest migrate to the account on sign-in, and that signing out starts a new guest.

Disable sign-in when no key is configured, where the identity calls would do nothing - do not show a signed-in account that the SDK knows nothing about. Use a demo user id that is not the raw email, and note in a comment that real apps pass their own backend user id and keep PII out of it.
acceptance_criteria: Vote as a guest, sign in, and the activity is attributed to the account; sign out starts a fresh guest; with no key the controls are disabled and explained.

title: Contextual feedback sheet from search and error states
description: Use FedoCreateFeedbackSheet as a lightweight submission entry point in two places: a "Missing a model? Request it" action in the no-results state, and a "Report a problem" action in the load-error state. Show these actions only when a key is configured (the SDK throws from the sheet when uninitialized). The sheet dismisses itself after a successful submit.
acceptance_criteria: Both actions open the sheet and submit successfully; with no key the actions are absent and nothing throws.

title: Roadmap destination hosting the Fedo feedback board
description: The Roadmap destination hosts FedoFeedbackScreen, wiring its onDismiss to the app navigation (it fires when the user backs out of the board root; the board owns its internal list/detail/editor navigation). When no API key is configured, show an app-level "Fedo not configured" state with setup instructions instead.
acceptance_criteria: With a key the board loads and voting/commenting works; without a key the setup guidance shows and nothing crashes.

title: Fedo SDK integration showcase
description:
Wire every public Fedo API into a natural moment of the app, so the repo doubles as integration documentation. Each integration point should be small, obvious and commented where the reason is not evident.

Important lesson from the iOS example: when no API key is configured, do not leave Fedo-backed UI reachable. The SDK cannot render a board without being initialized, so the app should show its own setup guidance and disable or hide the Fedo entry points instead of presenting something that silently does nothing.

title: App navigation scaffold
description: Three destinations reachable from a bottom navigation bar: Models, Roadmap (the Fedo board) and Settings. The models list and detail live under Models. Keep each destination self-contained so the Fedo screens can own their internal navigation and back behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: All three destinations are reachable; system back behaves correctly from the detail screen and from the Fedo board.

title: Model detail screen
description: Opened from a list row: short name and provider, input/output price per 1M, context length, release date, input modalities, the full description, and the model id shown in a monospace style with a copy action.
acceptance_criteria: Every row opens a detail screen with correct values; long descriptions scroll; copy puts the id on the clipboard.

title: Search and provider filter
description: Search matches model name or id, case-insensitively. A filter control lists providers with a model count each, most models first. Group by the stable providerID, not the display name, so a refresh that renames or drops a provider cannot strand the filter with zero matches; clear a selection that no longer exists. Ids that share a display name merge into one entry. When search or filter matches nothing, show a distinct no-results state (not the empty-data state).
acceptance_criteria: Search and filter combine; each provider appears once; after a refresh that drops the selected provider the filter recovers instead of showing permanent no-results.

title: Models list screen
description: Newest models first, with loading, error and empty states and pull-to-refresh. A failed refresh must keep already-loaded data and say so inline (do not wipe the list, do not fail silently). Only one load may run at a time: a new load cancels/supersedes the in-flight one so the initial load, refresh and retry cannot race. The error state offers Retry; the empty state offers Refresh. Row shows short name, provider display name, relative release date, context label and input price per 1M.
acceptance_criteria: List shows newest first; offline shows an error state with Retry; a failed refresh with data present shows an inline notice and keeps the list.

title: OpenRouter client, model type and formatters
description:
Model type decoding the subset above, tolerant of null/missing optional fields. Derived values: release date, provider display name (name prefix before ": " else id prefix with "~" stripped), a stable lowercase providerID grouping key, short name, price per 1M tokens as a display string, context label.

Formatting rules (from the iOS example): "0.00000096" -> "$0.96", "0.000000075" -> "$0.075", "0.000015" -> "$15", "0" -> "Free", "-1"/unparsable -> "Variable", and anything above 0 but below $0.01 per 1M -> "<$0.01" (never "$0"). Context: 1_048_576 -> "1M", 200_000 -> "200K", 131_072 -> "131K", 32_768 -> "32K", 512 -> "512".

Fetch function returns models sorted newest first and throws on non-2xx. Keep decoding/formatting as pure functions so they can be unit tested without the network.
acceptance_criteria: Fetching decodes all live models; formatter and grouping functions are pure and callable from tests.

title: ModelPulse core app
description:
Browse the newest AI models from the public OpenRouter API: GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (no key, ~445 models).

Each data[] entry has: id ("anthropic/claude-opus-5", sometimes "~" prefixed), name (often "Provider: Model"), created (unix seconds), description, context_length (nullable), pricing.prompt / pricing.completion (USD per token, as STRINGS; "0" = free, "-1" = variable), architecture.input_modalities ([String]).

Keep the app small and readable - it is documentation for SDK integrators. Put logic (decoding, formatting, filtering) in plain testable functions, not inside composables.

title: Decide the release build optimization settings
description: app/build.gradle.kts sets release { optimization { enable = false } }, so the release build is not minified or shrunk, with no note saying why. This is no longer cosmetic: the Fedo SDK leaks its test dependencies onto the runtime classpath (see the separate bead), and shrinking is what would strip them from a release APK. Either turn optimization on and supply the keep rules the app needs (app/src/main/keepRules/rules.keep already exists), or record why it stays off for an example app.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: the release build type's optimization setting is either enabled with working keep rules, or accompanied by a comment stating why it is off. AC-2: :app:assembleRelease succeeds and the app starts. AC-3: the decision is recorded in specs/decisions/.
close_reason: R8 enabled on release; strips the SDK's leaked test deps (46MB debug -> 2.5MB release, no junit/MockEngine in dex). Decision in specs/decisions/0002-release-optimization.md. Closed ahead of 8nq.6: that bug is an upstream SDK publication fix in another repo and does not gate this decision.

title: Decide the string resource and accessibility rules
description: No project rule says whether user-facing text lives in strings.xml or as literals in composables, and none covers contentDescription, touch target sizes or TalkBack. This matters now because specs/testing.md has UI tests matching literal text ('Retry'), which only works if that text is stable and reachable. Decide both and add them to the constitution.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: the constitution states where user-facing strings live. AC-2: the constitution states the minimum accessibility bar (contentDescription on actionable icons, touch targets, and how UI tests should locate nodes).

title: Give every acceptance criterion an ID
description: The constitution requires every acceptance criterion to carry an ID (AC-1, AC-2, ...) and to map to at least one test named after that ID. Existing beads state acceptance criteria as freeform prose, so the rule cannot be enforced or checked. Rewrite the acceptance field of every open bead into numbered criteria. Keep the wording; only add the IDs and split multi-part sentences into separate criteria.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: every open bead with acceptance criteria uses the 'AC-n: ...' form. AC-2: criteria that state two independent behaviours are split into separate IDs.

title: Settle the feature-spec workflow
description: CLAUDE.md still says feature specs live in specs/features/NNN-name/ (spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md), but the Workflow section no longer contains the rule that produced them ('Non-trivial feature: spec.md -> plan.md -> after approval, file an epic'). The directory does not exist and all four epics were filed without specs. Decide: either restore the spec-first rule and backfill specs for the open epics, or drop the specs/features/ reference and let beads be the only place features are described.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md describe exactly one feature workflow, with no reference to a directory that does not exist. AC-2: if spec-first is kept, specs/features/ exists and each open epic links its spec path.

title: Reconcile AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
description: The two agent instruction files have drifted. AGENTS.md carries a Beads codex setup block and non-interactive shell rules that CLAUDE.md lacks; CLAUDE.md carries the Build & Test, Architecture Overview and Conventions sections that AGENTS.md lacks. Beads' own guidance says mirror substantive edits across both or symlink one to the other. Pick one approach and apply it so agents reading either file get the same rules.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md contain the same project rules (verified by diff, or by one being a symlink to the other). AC-2: no section present in one file is missing from the other.
close_reason: Merged both files into AGENTS.md; CLAUDE.md is now a symlink to it. Also lifted the project-owned ## Specs section out of the managed BEADS INTEGRATION block so a bd regeneration cannot delete it.

title: CI guard against committed secrets
description: Fail the build if an API key is ever committed: check that local.properties is not tracked and that no tracked file assigns a non-empty FEDO_API_KEY. Print a message telling the contributor to use local.properties and to rotate a leaked key. This is cheap insurance - on the iOS example a real key sat in a tracked config file during development.
acceptance_criteria: The guard fails on a planted fake key or a tracked local.properties, and passes on a clean tree.

title: Set up CI
description: On pushes and pull requests to the default branch: set up JDK, cache Gradle, then assemble the app and run the unit tests. It must pass with no API key present. Treat compiler warnings as errors so the zero-warning rule the contributing guide states is actually enforced, and pin actions by commit SHA. Consider adding Android Lint.
acceptance_criteria: CI is green on the default branch and the README badge points at it.

title: Write the contributing guide
description: How to build and run (including the optional API key), how to run unit tests, code style and guidelines (keep the example minimal and readable, no unnecessary dependencies, no warnings, add tests for logic changes), branch and pull request flow, that maintainers plan with beads, and where to report: this repo for the example, the Fedo SDK repo for SDK bugs, SECURITY.md for vulnerabilities.
acceptance_criteria: Covers setup, tests and PR flow; linked from the README.

title: Add a CHANGELOG
description: Keep a Changelog format with an Unreleased section, and state which Fedo SDK version each release targets.
acceptance_criteria: CHANGELOG exists and lists the first release contents.

title: Write the README
description: Sections: what the example is and what it demonstrates, screenshots, requirements (Android Studio / AGP / Kotlin / minSdk / Fedo SDK version), quick start (clone, add FEDO_API_KEY to local.properties, run; note it also runs without a key), a "Where Fedo is used" table mapping each SDK API to the file that uses it, a note that Fedo keys are client-side keys shipped inside the app so local.properties only keeps them out of git, project structure, how to run tests, links to getfedo.com and the docs, contributing/security/conduct links, credit to OpenRouter for the model data, and the license. Badges: CI, license, platform.
acceptance_criteria: A new developer gets from clone to running app using only the README; every API in the table links to real code.

title: Capture screenshots for the README
description: Emulator screenshots of: models list, provider filter, model detail, settings, and the Fedo board with the create-feedback sheet (the board needs a configured key). Light and dark for at least the list and detail. Store compressed (a few hundred KB each) under a docs/images folder. Use a clean status bar (demo mode) so the images look deliberate.
acceptance_criteria: Images under ~300 KB each, consistent device and theme, referenced by the README.

title: Repo docs and health
description: The files and automation a public example repo is expected to have, so it is easy to find, run, trust and contribute to.

title: Set a favorite_provider user property from the filter
description: When the user picks a provider in the filter, record it with setUserProperty("favorite_provider", <display name>) so the dashboard can segment feedback by what the user cares about. Comment that properties are user-level and the last value wins.
acceptance_criteria: Picking a provider updates the property (visible with debug logging and in the dashboard).

title: Unit tests for decoding, formatters and filtering
description: JVM unit tests (no network, no emulator) over an inline JSON fixture shaped like real OpenRouter data: normal pricing, free ("0"), variable ("-1"), an entry with null context_length and no pricing/architecture, "~"-prefixed ids, and a model whose name has no "Provider: " prefix. Cover: newest-first ordering, tolerance of null/missing fields, every price and context formatting rule, provider/providerID/short-name derivation, provider grouping (ids sharing a display name merge, e.g. meta + meta-llama -> one "Meta" entry) and search combined with a provider filter.
acceptance_criteria: ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest passes; breaking a formatter makes a test fail.

title: Test on the oldest supported Android version
description: Run the app on an emulator at the minimum supported API level (and one mid-range level), checking the list, detail, board, sheet and settings. Compile-time checks do not catch behaviour differences on older platform versions.
acceptance_criteria: Core flows verified on the minimum supported API level.

title: Cut the first release
description: Decide the version (the Fedo product line shares its X.Y across SDKs, so matching the Fedo SDK minor version is the consistent choice), set the app version name to match, move the CHANGELOG Unreleased section into a dated release section, tag it, and publish a GitHub release with notes and screenshots.
acceptance_criteria: Tag and release published, with app version, CHANGELOG and screenshots in agreement.

title: Set the GitHub repo metadata
description: Repository description, website, topics (android, kotlin, jetpack-compose, feedback, feature-voting, fedo, sdk-example, openrouter) and a social preview image from the screenshots. Needs repo admin rights.
acceptance_criteria: Repo page shows the description, topics and preview image.

title: Fill in the agent instruction files
description: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md still carry template placeholders. Replace them with real build and test commands, a short architecture map (which file does what, and where each Fedo API is used), and the project conventions (minSdk floor, no unnecessary dependencies, zero warnings, key handling, keep the example minimal). Keep any managed beads blocks byte-for-byte intact and keep the two files consistent with each other.
acceptance_criteria: No placeholder text remains; commands in the files actually work.

title: Add issue forms, PR template and dependabot
description: Bug report and feature request issue forms (bug form asks for Android version, device/emulator, app commit and Fedo SDK version, and warns against pasting keys), a pull request template with a checklist (builds, tests pass, CHANGELOG updated, no secrets, screenshots for UI changes), contact links pointing SDK issues and documentation elsewhere, and a dependabot config for gradle and github-actions.
acceptance_criteria: New issue and PR pages show the templates; the dependabot config is valid.

title: Add Code of Conduct and security policy
description: Contributor Covenant 2.1 with a working private reporting route (no personal email addresses). SECURITY.md: supported versions, how to report privately, what to include, and an explicit warning never to paste API keys or local.properties contents into issues, plus where to report SDK vulnerabilities instead.
acceptance_criteria: Both files present and GitHub community standards satisfied.

title: Light and dark theme pass
description: Verify the app in light and dark themes (and dynamic color where the platform provides it), fixing any hardcoded colors. The Fedo screens follow the app theme, so this also decides how the SDK UI looks.
acceptance_criteria: Both themes render correctly with no hardcoded colors; screenshots exist for both.
